Primitive Instances inherit a base class of operational logi
Distribution attribution rests on a per-Instance Reward Code
First-party Instances omit the counterparty payment document

title: Each distribution partner gets its own Primitive Instance and Configuration Document rather than sharing global terms
content:
Every entry in the Distribution Reward Primitive's directories resolves to a distinct Instance Configuration Document — "Sky.money App Instance Configuration Document", "DeFi Saver Instance Configuration Document", "CoW Swap Instance Configuration Document", and so on (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.1.2.1 onward). There is no single global reward policy document that the venues are subordinate to.

The Instance is therefore the unit of commercial relationship. Because each Instance carries its own Parameters and Operational Process Definition, terms can differ per venue, and a change to one relationship is an edit to one Instance rather than a renegotiation of a shared policy.

The lifecycle machinery then applies per relationship as well: an Instance can be Active, Completed, Suspended, or the residue of a Failed Invocation, independently of every other. Ending a partnership means moving one subtree, not editing a list.

The cost is scale. Twelve venues at various stages already generate twelve document trees inside a single primitive, and the Artifact grows linearly with commercial activity. The Atlas accepts that in exchange for having each deal individually addressable, auditable and revocable — which is what allows a distribution program to be governed through the same Root Edit process as everything else.
description: Per-venue Instances make reward terms individually negotiable, separately amendable and separately terminable, at the cost of the Artifact carrying one document tree per relationship.
